articles.title: 3 dead in midair crash of 2 helicopters near Oregon airport: Sheriff
articles.summary: The incident occurred near McMinnville Municipal Airport.
articles.body:
Three people are dead after two helicopters collided in midair near an Oregon airport on Thursday, according to local authorities.

The incident involved a 1995 Robinson R22 helicopter and a 2018 Airbus AS350B3 helicopter and occurred at approximately 2:10 p.m. local time Thursday near McMinnville, about 40 miles southwest of Portland, according to the Yamhill County Sheriff's Office.

The sheriff said flight instructor Maddie Aasbo, 22, of Texas, and a student pilot from the U.K. were aboard the Robinson R22. The name of the student pilot was not released as authorities were working with the consulate and the FBI to notify family, the sheriff said.

The sole occupant of the Airbus AS350B3 was identified as Tyler Delane Sturdevant, 38, of Newberg, Oregon.

The sheriff's office said witnesses reported the collision near the intersection of Highway 33 and Cruickshank Road southeast of McMinnville.

When first responders arrived, they saw both aircraft crashed in a field near the highway.

The Federal Aviation Administration and the National Transportation Safety Board responded to the scene and are leading the investigation into the crash, the sheriff said.

The NTSB will lead the investigation, the FAA said earlier.

In an earlier statement, the FAA said there was one occupant aboard the Robinson helicopter and two people aboard the Airbus. The sheriff told reporters at a news conference that received his information from responding personnel.

ABC News' Amanda Morris contributed to this report.

articles.title: Man buys Ola electric scooter for Rs 1.02 lakh in January 2024, finds parking lock faulty on day 1 and vehicle stops working on day 2; consumer forum orders company to replace scooter or refund full amount with 10% annual interest
articles.summary: AGRA: An electric scooter that developed problems on the day it was purchased and stopped working completely the following day has landed Ola Electric
articles.body: AGRA: An electric scooter that developed problems on the day it was purchased and stopped working completely the following day has landed Ola Electric Technology Pvt Ltd in trouble, with an Aligarh consumer forum directing the company to replace the vehicle or refund its purchase price of Rs 1,02,505 with 10% annual interest.The Aligarh District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum also directed the company and its authorised service centre to pay Rs 10,000 as compensation for mental harassment and Rs 5,000 towards litigation expenses.Vaibhav Sharma bought the electric scooter from an Ola showroom on Jan 31, 2024, for Rs 1,02,505. On the first day itself, the vehicle's parking lock became engaged and could not be unlocked, while its storage compartment failed to lock after being opened.Sharma reported the defects to the Aligarh service centre and emailed the company's customer support team on Feb 1, his lawyer Shivam Nayak said on Thursday. The scooter stopped working completely the following day.According to the consumer forum's order, Sharma visited the service centre repeatedly on Feb 2, 3, 5 and 6, but the problems remained unresolved. He eventually had to leave the scooter at the workshop.On Feb 9, Sharma discovered that the company had closed his complaints without fixing the defects. He subsequently approached the consumer forum, seeking a replacement or refund, along with compensation for financial loss and mental harassment.In their joint written statement, Ola's manufacturing and service entities claimed they had taken all necessary steps to address Sharma's concerns promptly.However, the forum observed that the companies had not specifically denied the defects, Sharma's repeated visits to the service centre or the complaints he had raised. It noted that Sharma had supported his allegations through an affidavit, while the opposite parties had failed to specifically rebut them.In its order dated Oct 16, 2026, the consumer forum, comprising president Hasnain Qureshi and member Purnima Singh Rajpoot, held that Sharma had established his case against the company and its authorised service centre.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Agra | Silver Rate in Agra | Bank Holidays in Agra | Public Holidays in Agra | Agra AQI | Weather in Agra | Petrol Price in Agra | Diesel Price in Agra | CNG Price in Agra | LPG Price in AgraStay updated with the latest Agra news. articles.title: Diljit Dosanjh concert: Delhi Metro services will run till midnight on October 30 to facilitate spectators, while traffic curbs will remain in place around Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium from 1pm to midnight
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi Metro services will be extended till midnight on Friday (October 30) across its network, except the Airport Express Line and Rapid Metro,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi Metro services will be extended till midnight on Friday (October 30) across its network, except the Airport Express Line and Rapid Metro, Gurugram, to facilitate the movement of around 70,000 spectators expected to attend singer Diljit Dosanjh’s concert at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium.The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) said additional train trips would be operated to help concertgoers return home after the event. Standby trains will also be kept ready to handle any unexpected surge in passenger traffic.The timings for purchasing QR tickets through the Delhi Metro Sarthi mobile app will also be extended by an hour in view of the revised service timings, the DMRC said.Additional staff, customer service personnel and customer facilitation agents will be deployed at JLN Stadium Metro station and key interchange stations to guide commuters and manage passenger movement.Security arrangements will also be strengthened at the station, with additional personnel, door frame metal detectors and enhanced screening measures to ensure the orderly movement of passengers.JLN Stadium Metro station, located on the Violet Line connecting Kashmere Gate and Raja Nahar Singh, is the nearest station to the concert venue. The DMRC has encouraged concertgoers to use Metro services to reach the stadium and return home, saying this would provide a convenient mode of transport and reduce dependence on private vehicles.Traffic restrictions around JLN Stadium from 1pmTraffic restrictions will be in place on several roads around Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium from 1pm until midnight on Friday for the 'Aura India Tour 2026' concert, the Delhi Traffic Police said.According to a traffic advisory, six diversion points have been identified, with two additional points to be activated if required.Bhishm Pitamah Marg, Lodhi Road, Lala Lajpat Rai Marg between Defence Colony and Lodhi Colony Flyover, Arch Bishop Marg, 4th Avenue Road and 5th Avenue Road are among the stretches where traffic movement will be affected.Restrictions will also be imposed on the Barapullah Flyover stretch between INA and Jangpura Metro Gate 2, Dayal Singh College Road and internal roads in CGO Complex and Lodhi Colony.At the Lodhi Road-Dayal Singh College Road intersection, vehicles will not be allowed to enter Dayal Singh College Road. articles.title: Why this US woman filled two homes with 13,201 frog-themed items after a tiny tree frog appeared in her kitchen in 1983
articles.summary: A tiny tree frog that appeared in Susan Burgos’s kitchen in 1983 sparked a passion for collecting that eventually earned her a Guinness World Records
articles.body: A tiny tree frog that appeared in Susan Burgos’s kitchen in 1983 sparked a passion for collecting that eventually earned her a Guinness World Records title. More than 4 decades later, the American woman has amassed 13,201 frog-related items, ranging from jewellery and clothing to toys, antiques and Christmas decorations. Her collection occupies 2 homes in Camarillo, California, including a second property with a large garage that she bought to store more of her growing collection. Burgos achieved the record on January 12, 2026, surpassing the previous mark of 10,502 items held by Sheila Crown of the UK. Guinness World Records featured her achievement in September as part of its coverage marking the release of Guinness World Records 2027. For Burgos, it all began with a small frog and a gold ring with emerald eyes.How a tiny tree frog in Susan Burgos’s kitchen started her collection in 1983Burgos began collecting frog-themed objects after discovering a tiny tree frog in her kitchen in 1983. Speaking to Guinness World Records, she recalled how the encounter inspired her first purchase, a gold frog ring with emerald eyes. “It stole my heart,” she said of the frog. That initial purchase became the beginning of a collection that continued to grow over the following decades. Burgos now looks for frog-related objects wherever she goes, including while travelling and browsing catalogues for new additions.Her collection reflects how a single encounter can develop into a long-running personal interest. What started with one piece of jewellery expanded into thousands of objects connected by a common theme. In its feature on Burgos’s record-breaking collection, Guinness World Records describes how she continued adding to her collection over more than 40 years.How Susan Burgos achieved the Guinness World Records title with 13,201 frog-related itemsGuinness World Records lists Burgos’s achievement as 13,201 items, with the record achieved on January 12, 2026. The total surpasses the previous record of 10,502 items held by Sheila Crown of the UK, putting Burgos 2,699 items ahead of the earlier mark. The organisation’s record page has a discrepancy in its summary field, which displays 13,021, but its accompanying text and September feature give the total as 13,201. The collection spans several categories, including frog-themed jewellery, toys, clothing and antiques. It also includes Christmas decorations, with Burgos having enough frog-themed ornaments to cover an entire tree.Despite the sheer number of objects, Burgos has a particular favourite. Asked to choose one item, she singled out an animated biker frog riding a motorcycle and singing “Kokomo” by The Beach Boys. “Well, one that springs to mind is an animated singing biker frog on a motorcycle that plays ‘Kokomo’ [by The Beach Boys],” she told Guinness World Records.The collection has also created a practical challenge: finding enough room to keep everything. Burgos’s original home could no longer accommodate the growing number of items, prompting her to buy a second property with a large garage for storage. Guinness World Records highlighted the collection in its September feature marking the release of Guinness World Records 2027.What the global decline of amphibians reveals about the animals behind the collectionWhile Burgos celebrates frogs through her collection, their real-life counterparts face serious threats. A study published in Nature on October 4, 2023, titled Ongoing declines for the world’s amphibians in the face of emerging threats, assessed 8,011 amphibian species and found that 40.7% were globally threatened. The researchers identified climate change as the leading driver of deteriorating conservation status since 2004, followed by habitat loss. The findings provide wider context for the animals that inspired Burgos’s decades-long collecting passion, although her collection is not itself a conservation initiative.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Renault Duster was insured for Rs 5.75 lakh when it caught fire on a Delhi road in 2019; seven years later, a consumer commission has ordered Bajaj Allianz to pay the full insured value, Rs 25,000 compensation and Rs 10,000 in legal costs
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A consumer commission in Delhi has directed Bajaj Allianz General Insurance to pay Rs 5.75 lakh to a car owner whose Renault Duster was
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A consumer commission in Delhi has directed Bajaj Allianz General Insurance to pay Rs 5.75 lakh to a car owner whose Renault Duster was completely gutted in a fire, after the insurer refused to settle his claim despite receiving the required documents. The commission also directed the insurer to pay Rs 25,000 as compensation and Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses.In its October 15, 2026, order, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, West District, Janakpuri, held the insurance company liable for failing to settle the claim for the total loss of the insured vehicle. It, however, dismissed the complaint against Renault Motors and NCR Motors India, the authorised service centre.How did the Renault Duster catch fire?According to the commission order, Pramod Kumar had purchased a Renault Duster RXL Diesel Plus 110 PS in 2014 and regularly got it serviced. He had insured the vehicle with Bajaj Allianz General Insurance under a policy valid from February 17, 2019, to February 16, 2020. The policy carried an insured declared value (IDV) of Rs 5.75 lakh, for which he paid a premium of Rs 24,132.On July 31, 2019, at around 10.37 pm, Kumar was driving the car home when it caught fire near a petrol pump in Kirti Nagar, Delhi. He called the police and fire brigade to the spot, but the vehicle was completely gutted.Kumar subsequently filed an insurance claim with Bajaj Allianz. The insurer sought several documents, including his driving licence, police complaint, fire brigade report, vehicle history, technical report from the manufacturer and details of the occupants in the car when the fire broke out.The complainant submitted the documents but the insurer refused to pay the insured amount of Rs 5.75 lakh. Aggrieved by the rejection, he approached the consumer commission seeking the IDV of the vehicle and Rs 5 lakh in compensation.What did the commission find?The bench comprising president Sonica Mehrotra and members Richa Jindal and Anil Koushal noted that the insurer had failed to appear before the commission or file a defence to challenge the complainant's evidence. The proceedings against the opposite parties were conducted ex parte after they failed to appear despite being given opportunities.The commission also took note of a vehicle examination report prepared by Techliner Expertise for Renault India. The report recorded the suspected cause of the fire as “Arcing formation in non-genuine wiring fitting in vehicle”, which led to the melting of surrounding parts and eventually the burning of the entire vehicle. It also ruled out a manufacturing defect."We, therefore, allow the complaint only against OP 2 for non-settlement of accidental claim of insured vehicle of complainant and direct it to pay the IDV of Rs. 5,75,000/- along with compensation of Rs. 25,000/- and Rs. 10,000/- towards litigation charges to the complaianant We exonerate OP 1 and 3 Manufacturer, Authorised Service Centre respectively for no deficiency made out against them," the commission said.The bench observed that the dispute concerned the insurer's failure to pay the claim for the total loss of the insured vehicle. Since Bajaj Allianz had neither appeared nor challenged the complainant's evidence, the commission accepted his case and allowed the complaint against the insurance company.What did the commission order?The commission directed Bajaj Allianz General Insurance to:Pay Rs 5.75 lakh, the insured declared value (IDV) of the Renault Duster.Pay Rs 25,000 as compensation.Pay Rs 10,000 towards litigation charges.Comply with the order within 30 days of receiving it.The commission exonerated Renault Motors, the manufacturer, and NCR Motors India, the authorised service centre, as no deficiency in service was established against them.

articles.title: Sardinian restaurants introduce phone-free family meals: Why 15 eateries are asking diners to put smartphones away
articles.summary: If you walk into a restaurant in Sardinia these days, especially with your family, you might find the mood a little different: it’s quieter, maybe, or
articles.body: If you walk into a restaurant in Sardinia these days, especially with your family, you might find the mood a little different: it’s quieter, maybe, or just more focused on the people right in front of you. 15 restaurants across the island have agreed to try something that, not so long ago, was just normal life: everyone comes to dinner, and for an hour or two, the phones go away. Real conversations, instead of everyone staring down at screens. That’s the goal behind “A tavola senza schermi,” which literally means, “At the table without screens.” It’s a month-long experiment, but it’s already sparked international curiosity.Now, this isn’t some strict ban with staff marching around and handing out penalties if you answer a text. Per The Guardian, the restaurants are asking, not ordering, their diners to stash away their phones. In fact, to help smooth the transition, they’re giving out little “get-together kits” like games, coloring pages, things to do together at the table. It’s important to note that no one is forced, and nobody will be shamed if they sneak a peek at their notifications. If anything, the hope is to make phone-free meals feel inviting and even fun, not like some new set of rules to grind through.What is happening in Sardinia: Inside the phone-free restaurant initiativeThe idea was championed by Anna Cau, Sardinia’s regional ombudsman for children and teens. She didn’t go at it alone; Italy’s hospitality federation, Fipe-Confcommercio, backed the plan. It’s supposed to kick off on November 1, 2026, and go for one month at participating restaurants around the island: places in big towns like Cagliari and Oristano, but also in smaller ones. They started out thinking it would be just eight restaurants, but so many wanted in that it grew to 15.When families show up, they’ll be encouraged to slip their smartphones out of sight and dive into the “Kit del Ritrovo.” Kids get games and drawing materials, while parents receive a leaflet about managing their children’s screen use: a little nudge, in other words, that the phone-free table isn’t just about killing time until the food arrives. There’s even a QR code in that leaflet, linking to practical tips from Italian pediatricians.Notably, it’s all voluntary. Nobody’s locking up anyone’s phone behind the register, and certainly no one’s policing the table. The whole purpose is to make unplugging for a meal something people want to do, not something they feel forced into by a bunch of wagging fingers.Why do Sardinian restaurants care?Well, walk into any place serving dinner these days, and you’ll probably find a family where everyone is physically present but mentally a world away: kids glued to TikTok, parents scrolling through work emails or Instagram. Sardinian educators, doctors, and parents worry about what that screen time is doing, especially for children and teens. Anna Cau sees this as something that shouldn’t fall entirely on parents’ shoulders. Communities themselves, she argues, have to pitch in to give kids chances to actually connect face-to-face and screen-free.Meals together were once natural opportunities to slow down, talk, and connect. Restaurant owners have noticed how rare that’s becoming. Emanuele Frongia, the president of Fipe-Confcommercio Sardegna, insists on adults leading by example. There’s not much point in telling kids to put their phones away if every grown-up at the table keeps theirs out. He sees restaurants as places for real connections, and he wants to restore that. And what’s even more telling: it’s not just families with little kids. Restaurateurs have talked about entire tables of adults sitting side by side in silence, everyone absorbed in their own feeds. The habit goes deeper than just trying to entertain fidgety children.What do paediatricians say about kids’ screen time?Pediatric experts are on board with the project. Osama Al Jamal, who heads the Sardinian branch of Italy’s pediatricians’ federation, says way too many parents don’t really see the hidden risks and rewards of all this digital technology. The worry isn’t just about how many hours kids spend on their devices, but also what they’re actually doing with that time. Those screens have a way of crowding out everything else that’s good for a growing mind and body: think sleep, friends, time outside, and more. The numbers are striking: almost every Italian teen has a smartphone, more than half keep it powered on night and day, and about one in four is starting to show signs of outright problematic use. The experiment isn’t about treating every kid as a tech addict, but clearly, the habits are changing fast.That said, nobody’s suggesting kids should live in a tech-free bubble. The point is to carve out a bit more space for offline life, for awareness, for those little ordinary moments that don’t happen if everyone’s lost in their own screen.What’s next?The pilot will run for a month, giving restaurants and organizers a chance to see if families actually enjoy dinner without digital distractions. If it works, Sardinia’s hoping others across Italy, and maybe beyond, will make phone-free tables part of the routine. Of course, one dinner without phones won’t magically fix the bigger challenges around tech and family life. But it might spark some new habits, or at least get people thinking. Maybe parents will realize kids aren’t the only ones who struggle to unplug. Sometimes, the grown-ups need help remembering how to talk with each other, too.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Local wisdom offers insights into dholes in Western Ghats
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Observations, tales, and cultural traditions of communities living alongside wildlife can offer insights that scientific monitoring may miss.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Observations, tales, and cultural traditions of communities living alongside wildlife can offer insights that scientific monitoring may miss.Two studies led by researchers from National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS-TIFR), Bengaluru, and Wildlife Conservation Society-India (WCS-India) have explored how local ecological knowledge can help understand the endangered Asiatic wild dog, or dhole, in the human-dominated landscapes of Western Ghats.India holds the world's largest population of dholes, among the most threatened large carnivores globally. The studies, conducted in Wayanad in Kerala and Valparai in Tamil Nadu, show that local people, plantation workers and forest personnel can provide information about the animals' movements, pack sizes, behaviour and interactions with other species. They also document the cultural significance of dholes, including their place in folklore and spiritual traditions.The first study, titled "Local Ecological Knowledge offers opportunities to study and monitor elusive carnivores in coexistence landscapes", was based on 476 interviews with local residents, plantation workers and forest department personnel across Wayanad and Valparai.Researchers collected information on dhole sightings, pack sizes, habitat use and interactions with domestic dogs, livestock and other carnivores. The reported pack sizes were broadly consistent with observations from earlier ecological studies.In Valparai, an informant network established during the research helped scientists locate dhole packs and record more than 30 hours of footage documenting their behaviour.The findings also offered insights into how dholes share space with people. Interactions between the animals and people were common in tea plantations, but reports of livestock attacks were extremely rare. Many respondents said dholes tended to avoid people.However, interactions with domestic dogs were reported more frequently, pointing to a possible avenue for monitoring competition and disease transmission between wild and domestic canids.The second study, titled "The hunting god: Vernacular knowledge on Asiatic wild dogs (Cuon alpinus) blends ecological insights with folklore in a shared agroforest landscape of India's Western Ghats", examined the relationship between communities and dholes in Valparai through interviews with 89 people, including residents of tribal settlements and plantation workers.Beyond documenting ecological observations, researchers recorded memories, stories, songs, beliefs and spiritual associations. Respondents described dhole behaviour, including coordinated hunting, pack communication, vocalisations, diet, breeding periods and use of different parts of the landscape.One of the study's notable findings was the cultural significance of the animals. In several tribal communities, dholes are known as "Vettaikara Apichi", loosely translated as "hunting gods". Researchers documented associations between dholes and forest deities, rituals, prayers, songs and oral traditions. Some stories portrayed them as protectors or as kin to people and domestic dogs.People expressed a mix of caution, curiosity, admiration and affection towards the animals. While close encounters could evoke fear, respondents generally described dholes as avoiding people. Some admired their agility, coordination and teamwork during hunts.The researchers also found that this knowledge may be disappearing. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Arab parties emerge as kingmakers in Israel's next government after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc fell short of a parliamentary
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Arab parties emerge as kingmakers in Israel's next government after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc fell short of a parliamentary majority, with their combined 19 seats potentially offering the opposition a path to power.However, disagreements within the opposition and uncertainty over cooperation with Arab factions could complicate efforts to form an alternative government.Israel's final election results confirmed that Netanyahu's Likud-led bloc secured 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, while the four main opposition parties won 48. The remaining 19 seats went to Arab factions, leaving all sides short of the 61 seats required for a majority.Israel Election Results 2026 Live UpdatesLikud emerged as the largest party with 27 seats, while opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar secured 21. The Joint List won 11 seats and Mansour Abbas's Ra'am secured eight, taking the combined strength of the Arab parties to 19.The results have put Arab parties at the centre of coalition negotiations, with their support potentially determining whether Netanyahu retains power or the opposition manages to form an alternative government.What are Arab parties likely to do?The two Arab political groupings have different approaches to participating in the next government, making their support far from guaranteed.Ra'am, led by Mansour Abbas, has previously participated in a governing coalition. articles.title: In 2020, conservation partners began securing Maine’s Chadbourne Tree Farm; six years later, more than 27,000 acres of working forest are permanently protected from development. The forest remains open to the public
articles.summary: More than 27,000 acres of forestland in western Maine have been permanently protected after a six-year conservation effort brought together environmental
articles.body: More than 27,000 acres of forestland in western Maine have been permanently protected after a six-year conservation effort brought together environmental organisations, state agencies and local land trusts. The achievement safeguards working forests, drinking-water resources and recreational access across a landscape near Bethel that could otherwise have faced fragmentation and development. According to Maine Public, the Bangor Daily News and The Conservation Fund, the October 2026 milestone builds on an initial acquisition in 2020 and extends conservation protections across the surrounding region. The protected land includes approximately 11,000 acres at the heart of Chadbourne Tree Farm. Crucially, the agreement does not remove the forest from productive use: timber operations can continue, and the land remains accessible to the public.A six-year effort to protect Maine’s forestsThe conservation initiative began in 2020, when The Conservation Fund and the Malone Family Land Preservation Foundation acquired nearly 14,900 acres of Chadbourne Tree Farm. The purchase gave conservation partners time to arrange permanent protections and prevent the property from being divided into smaller parcels for potential development.The effort subsequently expanded beyond the original acquisition, bringing together Mahoosuc Land Trust, Greater Lovell Land Trust, Western Foothills Land Trust, Inland Woods + Trails, state conservation agencies and the US Forest Service. Together, the partners secured additional properties, expanded existing nature preserves and added land to public conservation holdings. The resulting network now protects more than 27,000 acres across western Maine.The broader initiative includes a 600-acre expansion of White Mountain National Forest, more than 1,300 acres added to Western Foothills Land Trust properties, and additional protected land along the Kezar River corridor. Mahoosuc Land Trust also secured substantial acreage, including the Crooked River Headwaters conservation easement and Tumbledown Dick Preserve.Protecting drinking water for more than 200,000 peopleOne of the most important benefits of the project lies in its watershed protections. Chadbourne Tree Farm sits near the headwaters of the Sebago Lake watershed, a critical source of drinking water for more than 200,000 people in the greater Portland area.Forests help protect water quality by filtering runoff, stabilising soil and reducing the movement of sediment into streams and rivers. Conserving large, connected forest areas can therefore help maintain the health of waterways that supply nearby communities. The protected landscape also provides wildlife habitat and forest corridors that allow animals to move through the region as environmental conditions change. Keeping these areas connected is particularly important as development and a changing climate put pressure on natural habitats.Working forests continue to support local jobsThe conservation agreement is designed to protect the land without ending its economic role. Chadbourne Tree Farm will remain an actively managed working forest, supporting timber production and jobs linked to Maine’s forest-products industry.The approach reflects a broader conservation strategy that seeks to balance environmental protection with the needs of rural communities. Rather than removing the land from economic use, the partners have secured its future while allowing sustainable forestry operations to continue.The project received support from Maine’s Land for Maine’s Future programme, the US Forest Service’s Forest Legacy Program, funding through the Land and Water Conservation Fund, and more than $10 million in private philanthropic contributions.A connected trail network for year-round recreationThe protected acreage also helps connect outdoor recreation areas around Bethel. Conservation of key parcels secures important sections of a continuous trail network linking Sunday River Resort and Mt. Abram, opening up opportunities for hiking, skiing and cycling throughout the year. The project also expands access to community forests, river corridors and other recreational areas used by residents and visitors.For western Maine, the achievement extends beyond the preservation of a single tree farm. It creates a connected landscape that supports clean water, working forests, wildlife and outdoor recreation while reducing the risk of future development fragmenting the region. Six years after the initial acquisition, the partnership has secured a long-term future for more than 27,000 acres, keeping the forest productive and accessible for generations to come.You use AI every day. articles.body:
India have already won the series, and New Zealand are running out of bowlers. The fourth T20I at Eden Park on Friday (12.30pm IST) will offer the hosts little comfort.

India chased 199 in 13.2 overs in Wellington, scoring 118 in the first six, the highest powerplay total in men's T20I history. Now they move to a ground where the boundaries are very short.

New Zealand vs. India prediction: Who will win?

India have scored at 10.45 an over across 38 T20Is this year, the best of any Full Member. New Zealand have managed 9.37 across 23 innings. Finn Allen apart, their batters do not hit with the same power, and their bowling attack has been stripped back further. Lockie Ferguson is out for the rest of the series, joining Matt Henry and Zak Foulkes on the injury list. Blair Tickner may play.

India have won 22 of their 34 T20Is against New Zealand, losing 11 with one tie, and they have taken eight of the last nine meetings. Their only real choice is how much to rest, with the ODI and Test series still to come. Kuldeep Yadav, Varun Chakravarthy and Shivam Dube have yet to play on this tour, and Mayank Yadav could return. Even so, the top order of Abhishek Sharma, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Sanju Samson and Shreyas Iyer would be hard for any attack to contain.

The Cricket News Prediction : India to win.

New Zealand vs India predicted lineups, team news for 4th T20I

India's one doubt is Ishan Kishan, who missed the second and third T20Is with a groin strain. Naman Dhir has settled quickly into international cricket, and his hitting has given the middle order extra power in the absence of Hardik Pandya.

Abhishek Sharma, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Sanju Samson (wk), Shreyas Iyer (c), Tilak Varma, Naman Dhir, Nitish Kumar Reddy or Shivam Dube, Kuldeep Yadav, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Prince Yadav, Arshdeep Singh

New Zealand are without Henry, Foulkes and Ferguson. Auckland's Bevon Jacobs could make his first international appearance at his home ground.

Finn Allen, Tim Seifert (wk), Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Bevon Jacobs, Michael Bracewell, Mitchell Santner (c), Adam Milne, Jacob Duffy, Matt Fisher, Blair Tickner
